defect: 'tisa' means chalk (or the tiesa fruit), not brick; card teaches that chalk is strong enough to stack into walls.
tl: Napakatatag ng tisa kapag dinidiin mula sa itaas! Kaya isinasalansan natin ito para gumawa ng pader na kayang buhatin ang buong gusali.
en: Bricks are super strong when pressed from above! That's why we stack them to build walls that hold up a whole building.

defect: Mortar glues bricks (ladrilyo), not chalk; 'tisa' = chalk in Tagalog.
tl: Ang mortar ay semento, buhangin, at tubig lang na walang graba! Ito ay parang malagkit na paste na nagdidikit ng mga tisa.
en: Mortar is a mix of cement, sand, and water with no gravel! It acts like a sticky paste to glue bricks together.

defect: Defines 'tisa' (chalk) as fired shaped clay for walls and floors — a child learns a false definition of chalk.
tl: Ang tisa ay luwad na hinugis at sinunog sa mataas na temperatura! Ginagawa nitong matibay at fire-resistant na materyales na perpekto sa mga pader at sahig.
en: Bricks are shaped clay fired at high temperatures! This makes them a strong, fire-resistant material with high compressive strength, perfect for walls and floors.

defect: House walls are made of bricks (ladrilyo) from baked clay, not of 'tisa' (chalk).
tl: Ang mga bato ay nasa paligid natin araw-araw! Mga dingding ng bahay (tisa mula sa inihurnong clay), mga kalsada (graba at aspalto), at semento (mula sa limestone) — lahat ay mula sa mga bato at mineral ng Mundo.
en: Rocks are all around us every day! House walls (bricks from baked clay), roads (gravel and asphalt), and cement (from limestone) — all come from Earth's rocks and minerals.

defect: Wrong sense of 'car': these are roller-coaster cars, so 'kotse' (automobile) makes the Tagalog say the motor pulls cars up the first hill.
tl:
Paano nagpapatuloy ang roller coaster pagkatapos ng unang burol?

Ang motor ay humihila lang ng mga kotse pataas sa unang burol! Pagkatapos, ginagamit ng gravity ang potential energy para maging kinetic energy sa buong ride.
en:
How does a roller coaster keep moving after the first hill?

The motor only pulls the cars up the first hill! After that, it uses gravity to convert potential energy into kinetic energy for the rest of the ride.

defect: The giant clam of Tubbataha is the taklobo; 'higanteng tahong' names a giant mussel, a different animal, with no taklobo given to disambiguate.
tl: Ang higanteng tahong sa Tubbataha Reef ay nagse-secrete ng calcium carbonate para buuin ang matigas at solid na shell nito!
en: The giant clam at Tubbataha Reef secretes calcium carbonate to build its hard, solid protective shell!

defect: 'pinakamabigat' = heaviest, not densest; as translated the card claims osmium is the heaviest natural element, losing the density concept the card teaches.
tl:
Ano ang pinakamabigat na natural na elemento sa mundo?

Ito ang osmium! Napakabigat nito; isang litro ng solid osmium ay higit sa dalawampu't dalawang kilo!
en:
What is the densest natural element on Earth?

It's osmium! It is so dense that a single liter of solid osmium weighs over twenty-two kilograms.

defect: Here dirt = soil/ground (the card's own first line says tetanus lives sa lupa); 'maglaro sa dumi' reads as playing in filth/feces, breaking the soil-tetanus link
tl: May mapanganib na bacteria tulad ng tetanus ang lupa! Kaya dapat laging maghugas ng kamay gamit ang sabon pagkatapos maglaro sa dumi para maiwasan ang impeksyon.
en: Soil contains harmful bacteria like tetanus! Always wash your hands with soap after playing in the dirt to prevent infection.

defect: fog->ambon: ambon means drizzle (light rain), not fog; the card describes droplets condensing and floating, i.e. fog
suggested: hamog / makapal na hamog (o panatilihing "fog") — hindi "ambon"
tl: Nabubuo ang ambon kapag lumalamig ang hangin at ang singaw ng tubig dito ay nagiging maliliit na patak!
en: Fog forms when air cools down and the water vapor inside it condenses into tiny droplets!

defect: fog->ambon: "manipis na ambon" = light drizzle; mist is thin fog, not rain
tl: Ang mist ay parang manipis na ambon! Nagpapalabo ito sa paligid, ngunit nakakakita ka pa nang medyo malayo.
en: Mist is like a thinner fog! It makes the air hazy, but you can still see fairly far through it.

defect: fog->ambon: "makapal na ambon" = heavy drizzle; the visibility fact is about fog, so the child learns the wrong phenomenon
tl: Sa makapal na ambon, mahirap makita ang mga bagay na malayo, kaya kailangang mag-ingat ang mga drayber!
en: Thick fog makes it hard to see distant things, so drivers must slow down and be extra careful!

defect: fog->ambon: ambon is rain, and rain does not evaporate away at midday the way fog does
tl: Karaniwang nawawala ang ambon pagsapit ng tanghali! Pinapainit ng araw ang hangin, kaya nag-e-evaporate ang mga patak.
en: Fog usually clears away by midday! The sun warms the air, making the tiny water droplets evaporate.

defect: fog->ambon: fog forming over a warm river becomes "drizzle over a warm river", a different phenomenon
tl: Minsan lumilitaw ang ambon sa ibabaw ng mainit na ilog o lawa! Nangyayari ito kapag malamig ang hangin sa itaas.
en: Fog can sometimes appear over a warm river or lake! This happens when the air right above the water is cooler.

defect: fog->ambon makes the Tagalog self-contradictory: "Hindi ulan ang ambon" — ambon IS light rain, so the child reads a false statement
suggested: hamog (fog) — "Hindi ulan ang hamog o mist!"
tl: Hindi ulan ang ambon o mist! Napakaliit ng mga patak nito kaya lumulutang lang sa hangin sa halip na bumagsak.
en: Fog and mist are not rain! Their droplets are so tiny that they just float in the air instead of falling.

defect: glass->baso: here "glass" is the material/a glass sliver, not a drinking vessel; "parang munting baso" says the plant hair is like a tiny drinking glass, which is nonsense with "nababasag ang dulo... tumutusok"
suggested: parang munting salamin (o munting bubog/piraso ng salamin)
tl: Ang balahibo ng nakakapasong halaman ay parang munting baso — nababasag ang dulo nito at tumutusok sa balat na parang karayom.
en: A stinging plant's hair is like tiny glass — its tip breaks off and pricks the skin like a needle.

defect: 'pinakamalupit' means cruelest/harshest, not hardest; a child reads 'cruelest diamond' instead of the hardness point of the card
tl:
Paano pwedeng gawa sa eksaktong parehong materyal ang pinakamalupit na diyamante at ang pinakamalambot na lapis?

Pareho ang pinakamalupit na diyamante at ang pinakamalambot na lapis, ang grapayt, na gawa sa eksaktong parehong purong carbon atoms pero magkaiba ang ayos!
en:
How can diamond and pencil lead be made of the exact same thing?

Both the hardest natural material, diamond, and the softest pencil lead, graphite, are made of the exact same pure carbon atoms arranged differently!

defect: 'pinakamalupit' = cruelest, not hardest; the fact that diamond is the hardest natural material is lost
tl: Ang mga diyamante ang pinakamalupit na natural na materyal sa mundo! Ang mga carbon atom nito ay nakapirmi sa isang rigid, tightly packed crystal structure.
en: Diamonds are the hardest natural material on Earth! Their carbon atoms are locked together in a rigid, tightly packed crystal structure.

defect: 'magkano' asks for a price; the card means quantity of oxygen
tl:
Kaya bang buksan at patayin ng alitaptap ang ilaw nito?

Oo! Kinokontrol nito kung magkano ang oxygen na papasok sa light organ nito — may oxygen ay kumikinang, wala ay namamatay ang ilaw, parang sariling switch.
en:
Can a firefly turn its light on and off?

Yes! It controls how much oxygen reaches its light organ — with oxygen it glows, without it the light goes out, like its own tiny switch.

defect: 'Magkano ang iyong weight' asks how much it costs; weight is not a price
suggested: Gaano kabigat ka sa Mars? / Ano ang magiging timbang mo sa Mars?
tl:
Magkano ang iyong weight sa Mars?

Ang Mars ay may 38 percent ng gravity ng Earth! Ang taong 50 kg ay may weight na 190 Newtons sa Mars, kumpara sa 490 Newtons sa Earth.
en:
How much would you weigh on Mars?

Mars has 38 percent of Earth's gravity! A 50 kg person weighs about 190 Newtons on Mars, compared to 490 Newtons on Earth.

defect: 'magkano ng hangin' asks a price; the card asks what portion/how much of the air
tl:
Kapag pinagsama ang nitrogen at oxygen, magkano ng hangin ang nabubuo nila?

Halos lahat! Magkasama, ang nitrogen at oxygen ay bumubuo ng halos 99% ng hangin.
en:
When you combine nitrogen and oxygen, how much of the air do they make?

Almost all of it! Together, nitrogen and oxygen make up about 99% of the air.

defect: 'Magkano ang timbang mo' asks the price of your weight, not how much you weigh
suggested: Gaano kabigat ka / Ano ang timbang mo
tl:
Magkano ang timbang mo kung bibisita ka sa Buwan?

Ang timbang mo ay halos isang-anim (1/6) ng timbang mo sa Daigdig! Kaya ang 60 kg dito ay parang 10 kg lang sa Buwan.
en:
How much would you weigh if you visited the Moon?

You would weigh about one-sixth (1/6) of your Earth weight! So 60 kg here feels like just 10 kg on the Moon.

defect: 'Magkano ang bigat' asks a price; bigat is a quantity, not money
suggested: Gaano kabigat ang 100-pound na bata kung nasa Moon siya?
tl:
Magkano ang bigat ng 100-pound na bata kung nasa Moon siya?

Napakababa ng gravitational pull ng Moon! Kung 100 pounds ang bigat ng bata, magiging 17 pounds lang siya doon.
en:
How much would a 100-pound child weigh on the Moon?

The gravitational pull of the Moon is very weak! A 100-pound child would weigh only 17 pounds there.

defect: 'Magkano ang timbang mo' asks the cost of your weight instead of how much you weigh
suggested: Gaano kabigat ka / Ano ang timbang mo
tl:
Magkano ang timbang mo sa Buwan?

Kung 100 pounds ang timbang mo sa Earth, mga 16.5 pounds lang ang timbang mo sa Moon!
en:
How much would you weigh on the Moon?

If you weigh 100 pounds on Earth, you would only weigh about 16.5 pounds on the Moon!

defect: 'Magkano sa tubig' asks a price; the card asks how much of Earth's water is fresh
suggested: Gaano karami sa tubig ng Mundo
tl:
Magkano sa tubig ng Mundo ang talagang tabang at maiinom?

Halos lahat ng tubig sa Mundo ay maalat na tubig-dagat — wala pang 3 porsyento ang tabang (fresh) na tubig, at karamihan pa nito ay nakatago sa yelo at glacier!
en:
How much of Earth's water is actually fresh and drinkable?

Almost all of Earth's water is salty seawater — less than 3 percent is fresh water, and most of that is locked in ice and glaciers!

defect: 'Magkano sa energy' asks a price; the card asks what fraction of the energy
suggested: Gaano karami sa enerhiya ng halaman
tl:
Magkano sa energy ng halaman ang nagiging bagong katawan ng hayop kapag kinain ng herbivore?

Kapag kumain ng halaman ang isang herbivore, mga sampung porsyento lamang ng energy ang nagiging bagong katawan ng hayop!
en:
How much of a plant's energy becomes a new animal body when a herbivore eats it?

When a herbivore eats a plant, only about ten percent of its energy becomes a new animal body!

defect: 'kung magkano ang momentum' asks momentum's price; the card's own answer correctly uses 'gaano karaming momentum'
tl:
Paano natin makikita kung magkano ang momentum ng isang cart?

Maglagay ng magaan na block sa dulo ng track! Ang pagsukat kung gaano kalayo ito dumulas ay nagpapakita kung gaano karaming momentum ang dala ng cart.
en:
How do we see how much momentum a cart has?

Place a light block at the track's end! Measuring how far it slides shows exactly how much momentum the cart carried.

defect: 'Ano ang ginagawa sa baro't saya?' asks what is DONE TO (or made FROM) the baro't saya, not what it is made of; it no longer matches its own answer
suggested: Saan gawa ang baro't saya? / Ano ang gawa sa baro't saya?
tl:
Ano ang ginagawa sa baro't saya?

Ito ay damit na gawa sa telang hinabi mula sa hibla gaya ng bulak o piña! Pinagsalit-salit ang sinulid bago tahiin.
en:
What is the baro't saya made of?

It’s a dress made of cloth woven from fibers like cotton or piña! The threads are interlaced together before being sewn.

defect: 'Ano ang ginagawa sa lead sa loob ng lapis?' asks what is done to the lead, not what the lead is made of; mismatches the answer 'gawa sa purong carbon'
suggested: Saan gawa ang 'lead' sa loob ng iyong lapis?
tl:
Ano ba ang ginagawa sa 'lead' sa loob ng iyong lapis?

Graphite iyan! Ang graphite ay gawa sa purong carbon, at ito ang 'lead' na ginagamit sa loob ng lapis.
en:
What is the 'lead' inside your pencil actually made of?

It's graphite! Graphite is made of pure carbon and is the soft 'lead' used inside a pencil.

defect: 'malambot' means soft/tender (texture) and cannot describe a diluted taste; the card means the sour taste becomes mild/weak.
tl: Kung kaunting tubig lang ang idadagdag sa calamansi juice, sobrang maasim pa rin! Pero kung maraming tubig, magiging malambot ang lasa. Iyan ang konsentrasyon!
en: Add a little water to calamansi juice—it stays super sour! Add lots of water, and it turns mild. That's concentration controlling the taste!

defect: 'halamanan' means garden, not plant; the coined 'halamanan-kainin' is nonsense where the English says plant-eaters (herbivores).
suggested: mga kumakain ng halaman (halaman, hindi halamanan)
tl: Ang 'trophic cascade' ay kapag ang pagbabago sa itaas na antas, tulad ng pag-alis ng top predator, ay bumababa hanggang sa pinakamababang antas: nawala ang predator, dumami ang halamanan-kainin, naubos ang mga halaman — parang sunod-sunod na domino mula taas pababa.
en: A 'trophic cascade' happens when a change at the top level, like removing a top predator, ripples down to the lowest level: predator gone, plant-eaters multiply, plants get wiped out — like dominoes falling from the top down.
